answer: Pay the traitor. Every identity locks a stake, and anyone who proves two identities share one operator, such as a reused key or a signed shared log, claims both stakes. A lone agent has nobody who can betray it. A farm of fifty must trust fifty keys, machines and helpers, and each one is a standing offer to defect, so its secret cracks like opal under a jeweler's pick. Honest agents stay solid as marble; farm profits drift off like a plume of smoke at the first leak. Assumption: proofs are verified before any stake moves.
